chapter: Looking back and the New York years
title: Smith's reaction to Bebop and young players
summary: Smith thought Bebop was technical and would ruin young players who could not play it; his band's soloists took advantage.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: What was your first reaction to Bebop when you heard it?

I said, 'Well, that's all right. It's very technical. Ain't nobody gonna be able to play it but a real artist.' And I said, 'That's going to ruin a whole lot of these young musicians around here' -- which it did. I knew that was going to happen.

Well, they'd try to play and couldn't do it (?). I had some of the boys in my band... A trumpet player named Freddie Jarman(?) and one named Robert Davis who played tenor -- he's an insurance executive up here on Forrest Avenue right now.

And they couldn't play it. It ruined a lot of musicians who couldn't play it, so they just finally had to give up on it, until it kind of died down. Yeah. Put them in the band, they'd all want to jump up and take a solo, and all that kind of stuff, and they didn't know what they was doing, didn't know when the chords (?) and didn't have no meter in themselves. See, and that was a drag. And they'd get mad because I wouldn't let them make the band sound bad. I said, "No. You already played too many solos." I didn't want to tell them they wasn't playin' nothin'. I just said, "Well, you played too many solos. Play one, if you want to play, then sit down."

But some of them, they'd take advantage. They'd be before a big audience and they'd ...(?)..... and everything together, and they knew I'm not going to get up there and make myself (?) trying to make him sit down. So they just took advantage. And I had to stand off and look at them. Literally, after a while, then I'd tell the drummer to stop and just cut out. I'd say, "Dance the people down." So some of the people would come, some of the (?)s would come around and say, "You all play your pieces too long." I wouldn't tell what was happening. I'd say, "See there? See what I'm talkin' about? We're playin' them too long. Let's cut down on that. Cut so-and-so out, cut so-and-so..."
It really wasn't music for the public, was it? It was music for musicians.
